correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed for every finite real scalar measure with nonzero atomless part: the scalar max identity gives a two-sided average exactly; the atomic band is ℓ1 with Schur, forcing weak-null atomic mass to zero. The diffuse Rademacher lemma follows from dyadic bisection and orthogonality in L2, with L1 approximation. Explicit scaled diffuse sign witnesses attain a+max(b,t) for b>0, and a disjoint diffuse unit function works at b=0. All quantifiers t≥0, ε≥0, endpoints a=0, b=0, and nonseparable measure algebras are treated. The all-measure claim rests on the analytic proof, not on finite verification.

originality.rationale: Compared implications, not keywords: arXiv:2301.07943 provides the purely nonatomic WASQ theorem and Rademacher lemma; arXiv:1705.06610 and 1402.0818 concern entire-space WASQ direct sums; Ciaci 2210.13306 concerns positive LASQ. value.rationale: The core theorem is the entire exact intrinsic weakly null two-sided norm profile of every unit point in classical mixed L1 spaces, not a routine special point calculation. It gives a natural complete classification of weakly almost-square points, optimal excess tolerance for all ε≥0, and sharp metric distance 2a to the locus. Its atomic/diffuse transition is structurally motivated by Schur versus Rademacher behavior, including quantitative stability beyond the previously known whole-space WASQ status.
